script.base: Books have NYJ 21.5 / MIA 18.0 in a 39.5 game, so a close, low-play script, not a shootout. Both offenses already run (Gordon 44 carries / Willis 19 carries in MIA weeks 3-5; Allen 55 carries in NYJ weeks 4-6). NYJ blitzes 37% and MIA EPA/dropback is -0.35 vs the blitz versus -0.03 with no blitz, so Miami's deep air (Washington 262 air yards, Bell 239) stalls and the workable throws are short middle to Dulcich.
script.flip1: NYJ scores early and leads by two scores. MIA abandons the run, Gordon's carries die, Willis is forced into more dropbacks against the blitz, and Washington/Bell target volume rises in a negative script while Allen salts the clock on the ground.
script.flip2: MIA's run game hits first (Gordon 5.2 YPC, Willis 7.4 YPC vs a NYJ defense allowing 4.38 YPC and 18 runs of 10+ in 6 games). Miami leads, NYJ throws more at a secondary missing CB Reese Taylor (Out) and possibly S Kyle Louis (Q), and Allen's rush line stalls. Weather is unknown and could also drag this into a lower slog.

matchup.pressure: NYJ blitz rate 37% and MIA is clearly worse when blitzed (EPA/db -0.35 vs -0.03). That pressure profile kills deep WR yards and should lift TE/RB checkdowns if drives survive. Explosive pass rate is modest on both sides; the soft spots are NYJ middle and MIA middle/left, plus NYJ's chunk-run allowance.
matchup.overlap: MIA's primary target is Malik Washington (23 targets, 166 yards, 262 air, about 11.4 aDOT). That deep profile does not attack NYJ's weak middle and runs into the blitz — negative overlap, not a bet. The real overlap is Dulcich (12 targets, 95 air yards, 92 yards) into NYJ's middle and a vacated LB. Gordon's 44/229 rushing overlaps the soft NYJ run numbers, but Willis already takes 19/141 and the blitz can flip Miami off the run. NYJ's primary, Garrett Wilson (21/175/179), overlaps MIA's middle/left bleed, but his 66 line has no two-sided price.

pre_mortem: Monday both leans lost because the blitz was drive-killers, not checkdowns: Dulcich finished 17-18 again while Willis ate sacks, and Bell still posted the one 40-plus gain he already showed he can (the 67), either on a broken coverage or once Miami trailed and aired it out. The other miss path is role: Bell's zeros were inactive/low-snap weeks and he played a real 12-target day, or Mauigoa being out was already in the 21.5 and Dulcich just split looks with Washington (23 targets) and Coleman (15). Hall playing or sitting does not decide these two, but a late Dulcich or Bell inactive would. Counter is strong enough that both stay leans, not strong.
slip_story: One story only: NYJ pressure in a 39.5 game. Short middle over (Dulcich) with the deep MIA under (Bell). They do not need a shootout. They are only partly correlated — dead drives help Bell's under and can miss Dulcich, so this is not a press-the-stack slip. Do not add Washington over, Bell over, a game over, or Gordon over (that needs the run script the blitz can flip). Allen is a separate NYJ-leads story and is blocked until Hall's inactive tag. No TDs, one market per player, two legs.
